item.title: ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29
item.description:
ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29

ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to address three critical vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages.

🔍 Overview

  • Control Center Express is a central dashboard used by IT administrators to monitor and remotely manage fleets of PCs.
  • The product is marketed to businesses and IT service providers and supports more than 200 ASUS business, workstation, and Corporate Stable Model motherboards.

⚙️ Fixed Vulnerabilities

CVE Severity Type Impact
CVE-2026-114202 Critical (CVSS 10.0) Hard‑coded cryptographic key Unauthenticated remote attacker can forge an authentication token and gain administrator privileges with no prerequisites
CVE-2026-114204 Critical Hard‑coded key Remote attacker with low privileges can forge a session token for a recently logged‑in account
CVE-2026-114205 Critical Authorization flaw Low‑privileged user can create an administrator account

🚀 Availability

  • Versions earlier than v1.7.29 are affected. The security bulletin lists versions through v1.7.27; the status of v1.7.28 is unclear.
  • Affected users should install v1.7.29, then update agents on managed devices via Select Function → Client Agent Updater and verify the agent versions.

📦 Related Updates

  • Control Center Enterprise and Control Center Datacenter received patches for CVE-2026-126574, a critical authorization flaw that lets a low‑privileged Viewer role change an administrator’s password.
  • Armoury Crate was updated to fix CVE-2026-112115, a high‑severity privilege escalation flaw affecting all versions up to 6.7.2.

💡 Why it matters

  • The unauthenticated remote exploit (CVE‑2026‑114202) provides full administrative control without any user interaction, representing a worst‑case scenario for enterprise IT environments.
  • Even the lower‑privilege flaws could enable attackers to elevate their access, potentially compromising large fleets of managed PCs.
  • Prompt patching is essential to maintain the integrity of the management console and the devices under its control.

#ASUS #Security #Vulnerabilities #ITManagement

Source: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express

item.title: Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error
item.description:
Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error

Devices that installed the November 2026 hotpatch update may experience errors when installing, launching, or running some applications. The error displayed is similar to “ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)”.

🧩 How it works

Current investigation suggests this issue occurs for applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, found as msi.dll. This can happen more frequently with 32-bit applications, but can also occur for 64-bit applications under certain conditions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Systems: This known issue impacts systems that have installed the hotpatch updates pushed through Windows Autopatch. It should not impact systems that have installed the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Workaround: Users must edit the Windows Registry to increase the HotPatchTableSize.
  • Registry Procedure:
    1. Open the Windows Registry by typing “regedit” in the Start menu and selecting Registry Editor.
    2. Navigate to the HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management folder.
    3. Locate the “HotPatchTableSize” registry key, open it, and set the Value to “2000”.
    4. Close the registry editor and restart the device.
  • Warning: Microsoft advised backing up the registry and ensuring knowledge of how to restore it before modifying it.

🚀 Availability

  • Windows Autopatch History: Microsoft first announced Windows Autopatch in April 2022, stating it would be available for free to customers with a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater starting in July 2022.
  • Public Preview: The feature reached public preview in early June and has been generally available since July 2022.
  • Default Policy: Microsoft stated in March that it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through the Microsoft Graph API and Microsoft Intune, after the May 2026 Windows security updates are installed.
  • Recent Fix: One month after the March announcement, Microsoft fixed a Windows Autopatch bug that caused driver updates restricted by administrative policies to deploy on some Autopatch-managed Windows devices belonging to customers in the European Union.

#Windows #Hotpatch #WindowsAutopatch #SecurityUpdates #Registry

Source: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch

item.title: CIOs Report AI Adoption Outpacing Governance, Highlight Authority‑Accountability Gap
item.description:
CIOs Report AI Adoption Outpacing Governance, Highlight Authority‑Accountability Gap

New research from Thoughtworks shows that AI adoption is moving faster than governance structures can keep up, creating a widening gap between authority and accountability for CIOs across North America.

🔍 Overview

  • Surveyed 3,200 CIOs across 10 countries.
  • 91% say AI adoption is outpacing governance.
  • The study highlights a growing mismatch between who has authority over AI decisions and who is held accountable for the outcomes.

⚖️ Authority vs. Accountability

  • Responsibility shift: 92% of North American CIOs now spend more time redesigning workforce workflows and labor models than managing core IT infrastructure (94% in the U.S., 91% in Canada).
  • CIOs are being held personally accountable for AI outcomes they cannot fully influence.
  • Incidents: 37% report security incidents involving AI systems; 35% cite data‑privacy breaches.
  • Perceived lack of authority:
    • Workforce disruption: 32%
    • Regulatory/compliance failures: 32%
    • Demonstrating ROI on AI: 31%
  • “AI governance is also a workforce design issue,” said Rachel Lycock, Chief Technology Officer at Thoughtworks.
  • “Authority over AI is distributed, but accountability hasn’t always moved with it,” said Mike Sutcliff, CEO of Thoughtworks.

📊 Governance & Budget Structures

Budget Responsibility Models (North America)

Model Share of CIOs
Budgets managed centrally by IT/technology 21%
Budgets controlled independently by business units 21%
Responsibility shared between IT and business 20%
Model still evolving 20%
Budgets managed centrally at executive/board level 19%
  • 92% of CIOs (94% U.S., 89% Canada) believe central IT will ultimately be held responsible for security or compliance failures caused by AI tools purchased by business units.
  • Thoughtworks emphasizes that the solution is not to re‑centralise every decision or to place a single executive in charge; instead, organizations need clearer decision rights and skilled people to make informed choices.

👥 Leadership & Roles

  • Chief AI Officer (CAIO) adoption:
    • 67% of surveyed organizations have already hired a CAIO.
    • 28% are planning to appoint one.
  • Relationship between CAIO and CIO/CTO is unclear:
    • 38% see the CAIO as an extension of the CIO/CTO’s centralized strategy.
    • 34% view the CAIO as operating independently with equal or greater enterprise influence.
    • 28% describe the relationship as a source of friction or unclear boundaries.
  • “At Thoughtworks, our experience has been that AI transformation is a team sport, from defining enterprise AI strategy and architecture to embedding AI into internal platforms and day‑to‑day operations.”
  • “The question isn’t who owns AI, but how leadership collaborates to create business value responsibly and at scale.”

📈 Next Steps & Confidence

  • Despite the gaps, 97% of CIOs consider their organization prepared to govern AI consistently across multiple business functions.
  • 66% describe their organization as very prepared (U.S. 83%, Canada 49%).
  • Planned actions (next 12 months):
    • 56% are establishing a formal AI governance and operating model.
    • 52% are embedding a dedicated technology lead within each business unit.
    • 48% are expanding the CIO’s role to oversee enterprise‑wide AI strategy and implementation.

#AIGovernance #CIO #EnterpriseAI #Thoughtworks

Source: 91% of North American CIOs say AI adoption is outpacing governance, leaving them accountable without control
